data.name: Moemen
data.gender_notes: Moemen is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Believer, one who trusts and relies on God
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic word ‘Amin’ which means ‘trustworthy’ or ‘reliable’. The name Moemen is derived from this root, meaning ‘believer’ or ‘one who trusts and relies on God’. This name is a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in Allah. The name Moemen carries the meaning “Believer, one who trusts and relies on God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Moemen usually hope their child will grow to embody believer, one who trusts and relies on god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the importance of faith and trust in Allah
data.etymology: Moemen belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Believer, one who trusts and relies on God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Moemen total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: معمن
in_arabic.long_meaning: المنعم بالخير والبركة، المعين بالحكمة، الموفق بالرزانة، والصادق بالصدق، هو الشخص الذي يتمتع بالخير والبركة، وينعم بالحكمة والرزانة، ويتسم بالصدق والوفاء، ويتطلع إلى التقوى والطاعة، ويحتفظ بالصبر والشكر، ويتمتع بالخير والبركة في الدنيا والآخرة.

in_urdu.name: معمن
in_urdu.long_meaning: منعم خیر وبرکت سے، معین حکمت سے، موفق رزانہ سے، صادق صادق سے، وہ شخص جو خیر وبرکت سے نوازا ہوتا ہے، حکمت و رزانہ سے معین ہوتا ہے، صادق و وفی سے مشہور ہوتا ہے، تقویٰ و طاعت کا مقصد بنتا ہے، صبر و شکر میں ہمہ وقت قائم رہتا ہے، اور دنیا اور آخرت میں خیر و برکت سے نوازا ہوتا ہے۔

historical_references.reference: Moemen was a prominent leader during the early Rashidun Caliphate and played a crucial role in the Battle of Siffin. He initially supported Caliph Ali (r. 656-661), but later renounced his allegiance and formed the Kharijite movement which rejected the authority of the caliph and demanded the application of the Quranic principle of 'qisas' (equality in retaliation). Moemen's rebellion led to a civil war, which was finally put down by Caliph Ali's general, Ibn A'as.
historical_references.context: Rashidun Caliphate, Battle of Siffin, Kharijite movement

historical_references.reference: Moemen ibn Saleh, also known as Ibn al-Dabbagh, was a scholar, theologian, and poet in the 8th century during the Abbasid Caliphate. He is best known for his work 'Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir' (The Comprehensive Dictionary), which is the oldest surviving Arabic dictionary and contains over 30,000 entries.
historical_references.context: Abbasid Caliphate, Scholar, Theologian, Poet, Arabic Dictionary
